audit.title: CCIP Tutorials (Aptos)

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Opens strongly — "Chainlink CCIP enables secure cross-chain communication between Aptos and EVM blockchains" is self-contained and liftable. Section leads ("Send messages and tokens from Aptos to EVM chains") are directional and clear. Weak point: sections are link lists, so a lifted chunk points elsewhere rather than answering in place.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong; 5 headings, 1 H1, 0 level skips, no section over 600 words (max 170). Clean H2 hierarchy and bulleted differences aid extraction. A summary table (see recs) would push this higher.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Weak — only 3 numerals, 0 with units, 0 version strings. No lane counts, chain selectors, fee details, or supported-network specifics. Expected on a tutorial hub but still limits standalone value.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 7 internal links, well-labeled, but 0 external/primary sources. No link to the CCIP concepts page, the Move/Aptos Fungible Asset standard, or the CCIP architecture spec despite defining those concepts.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Good — the "Key Differences from EVM" and "Message Types" bullets are crisp, verbatim-liftable definitions (Account Model, Resource Model, Programmable Token Transfers). Near-first-use and self-contained.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak — 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no `dateModified`/`inLanguage` in `<head>`. A body "Last Updated: 2025-09-03" exists but is not machine-exposed. The `<head>` was not captured; CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a full read.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No code — acceptable for an index page, so this is context-limited rather than a true failure. A minimal orientation snippet (e.g., the CCIP message struct) is not expected here.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers directional flows and message types, but headings are concept-titled, not query-phrased. No "How do I send a token from Aptos to Ethereum?" or error/symptom coverage.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; consistent naming ("CCIP", "Aptos", "EVM", "Move"), unambiguous prose, no undefined jargon. No action needed.

audit.summary: This is a navigational hub page indexing the CCIP↔Aptos tutorial set, not a deep technical guide — judged against best-in-class *index* pages, it is clean and well-structured but thin on the machine-readability and specificity signals that drive citation. Its biggest strength is a crisp answer-first opener and a scannable "Key Differences from EVM" section that engines can lift verbatim. Its biggest opportunity is metadata: no JSON-LD, no canonical URL, and no in-`<head>` date leave it hard for agents to trust and rank. Honest verdict: functional as human navigation, under-optimized as an agent-retrievable entry point.

recommendations.title: Add query-phrased headings/anchors
recommendations.where: "Using Aptos as a Source Chain" / "Using Aptos as a Destination Chain"
recommendations.issue: headings are concept-titled, not how devs ask.
recommendations.change: add H3 sub-anchors or reword to intent form, e.g. "How to send tokens and messages from Aptos to EVM chains" and "How to send from EVM chains to Aptos." Keep the current label as a secondary line.
recommendations.why: devs/agents query by task ("how do I send from Aptos to Ethereum"); intent-phrased headings win retrieval that concept titles lose.

recommendations.title: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with canonical + dates
recommendations.issue: 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no machine-readable date.
recommendations.change: add JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified: 2025-09-03`, `inLanguage: en`, and a canonical `<link>` to the non-`.md` URL.
recommendations.why: structured metadata and visible freshness raise parse-ability and trust; canonical prevents `.md`/HTML duplication ambiguity.

recommendations.title: Add a summary comparison table
recommendations.where: top of page, after the intro sentence
recommendations.issue: direction/message-type options are scattered across four sections.
recommendations.change: insert a small table — columns Direction | Guide | Token Transfers | Test networks used — so an engine can extract the option matrix in one chunk.
recommendations.why: tables let engines build justified, structured answers and improve chunk retrievability.

recommendations.title: Add external/primary citations for defined concepts
recommendations.issue: defines Move resource model and Fungible Asset standard with 0 external links.
recommendations.change: link "Fungible Asset standard" and "Move language" to the canonical Aptos docs, and link "CCIP" to the CCIP concepts page.
recommendations.why: inline authoritative links raise credibility and citation rate.

recommendations.title: Add concrete specifics to the testnet note
recommendations.where: the NOTE block ("Aptos Testnet and Ethereum Sepolia testnet")
recommendations.issue: only 3 numerals on the page, no units or identifiers.
recommendations.change: name the CCIP chain selectors / network identifiers for Aptos Testnet and Sepolia, and link the supported-networks reference.
recommendations.why: quantitative, specific identifiers are among the highest-lift changes for citation.

recommendations.title: Add a short "What is CCIP on Aptos?" lead definition
recommendations.issue: intro is one sentence; no bounded definition an engine can quote as the canonical answer.
recommendations.change: add a 2-sentence definition stating what CCIP enables between Aptos and EVM and which message types are supported.
recommendations.why: a crisp first liftable sentence defends against parametric-prior substitution when the page is skimmed.

antiPatterns: None material. Prose is clean, dated (in body), and free of marketing fluff or unresolved cross-references. The only gap is structural/metadata thinness, addressed above — not a stylistic anti-pattern.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced — good site-level signal; ensure this hub and its child tutorials are listed there.
Canonical URL and JSON-LD are template-level concerns; fix once in the site layout to benefit all tutorial hubs.
`<head>` metadata could not be verified from the supplied content; pass raw `<head>` in the CLI for a definitive machine-readability read.
